Revised assessment using SLOOS: While the FOMC’s March 15, 2020 statement emphasizes aggressive easing (ZLB, large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, expanded repo, discount window, and dollar swap lines) to support market functioning and credit flow, the SLOOS points to a meaningful tightening in the supply of bank credit and weaker demand that deepen downside risks.

Key SLOOS takeaways reinforcing a more negative tone:
- Banks tightened lending standards and other terms, notably for C&I and construction/land development loans; reduced credit limits and raised credit score thresholds (Refs: 7, 19, 21, 22; 0, 8).
- Demand weakened in key segments (consumer; construction and land development), and banks reported/expect further tightening for riskier loans and across C&I, multifamily, and CLD (Refs: 11, 20; 13, 31, 30, 33).
- Banks expect reduced risk tolerance and deterioration in loan portfolios, collateral values, and HELOC performance (Refs: 14, 27, 28, 29).

Combined with the FSR’s highlighted pre-pandemic vulnerabilities (elevated corporate leverage, nonbank funding risks, and Treasury market fragility), these SLOOS insights imply tighter financial conditions and greater tail risks than a macro-only read, even with Fed backstops.

Net effect: downgrade the tone from the prior -0.30 to reflect tighter bank credit supply and expected deterioration.
